app.name: WiiKart
app.long_description: Semi-sim racing over nine circuits: seven stylized Colorado mountain passes with real grades, switchbacks, cliffs, and gravity, a flat speedway, and a wide, barriered oval with grandstands and real, gentle banking in its turns. Every circuit has its own weather (snow that melts into ice and then a puddle, with soft, medium, and hard tires each suited to a different stage) behind a race-setup toggle, off by default. Every circuit's curves cant into the bend and genuinely add cornering grip, and cars themselves visibly bank with the road. Grip holds until you deliberately break it loose with the handbrake, no surprise spins from steering alone. Every car has one real engine curve, peaking at a single nominal RPM shared by every gear, and is naturally aspirated, turbocharged (real lag), or supercharged (instant, smaller bonus). Eleven fallible AI rivals use different strategies and driver personalities, learn from mistakes, adapt without rubber-banding, hunt the real racing line every track's own geometry hints at rather than a fixed position, and range from careful to three no-guts-no-glory drivers who commit to everything and pay for it in falls — skill itself now shows up as how tightly a driver holds that line and how fully it capitalizes on a cover or an attack, not just how much grip it dares to use. Every car has its own drivetrain — front, rear, or all-wheel drive with a tunable front/rear bias. Thirteen cars in the garage, each looking like its own numbers, edit any of them (built-ins included) or design your own from scratch with full control of gearing and aspiration (mass and grip follow power and drag as real trade-offs). No collectible power-ups. Every on-screen speed, distance and weight reads in mph, feet and pounds. Cars, game settings, and keyboard/GameCube/Xbox control guidance are editable in documented JSON files. Includes lap timing and a live leaderboard, a marshal helicopter for driving the wrong way, an optional Dolphin input translator, per-track lap counts, garage, manual gearboxes, tire strategy, staged cliff recovery, up to 4-player split screen, and procedural audio. Supports Wii Remote, Nunchuk, Classic Controller, GameCube pads, Xbox pads through Dolphin, and USB keyboard. Runs on Wii hardware and in Dolphin.
